findings.title: Criterion 20 is not assigned to P08 in the ownership map
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 5 pass condition: “Criterion 20 owned by P08.”
findings.trigger: The authoritative ownership table is used to determine the primary owner of Criterion 20.
findings.consequence: Criterion 20 is dispatched to P00A rather than the required P08 clean-room release prompt, and the document contains conflicting ownership declarations.
findings.evidence: In `acceptance_criteria_mapping.v1.md`, the ownership table maps Criterion 20, “Inventory reproducibility,” to P00A, and the ownership summary repeats `P00A | 20`. The Authority Notes then contradict the table by saying Criterion 20 is complete end-to-end verification owned by P08. The checkpoint criterion explicitly requires Criterion 20 to be owned by P08.

observations: The mapping now accurately reproduces the titles of specification §10 criteria 1–20 and gives every table row one owner; this resolves the specification-faithfulness portion of the prior finding.
The P02S ownership and authorized-path repairs remain effective, and the original v3 prompt remains unmodified.

Generated P02S v4 still has an incorrect relative schema directive after relocation, and the checkpoint still lists its obsolete root-level path under “FILES CREATED.” These do not independently defeat the narrowly stated blocker criteria.
reasoning: The record matches all three verdicts I previously issued. Most prior defects are repaired, but the remaining acceptance map directly violates Criterion 5’s explicit required assignment for Criterion 20 and is internally contradictory about that owner. Because every stated criterion must pass, this surviving blocker requires FAIL.
